source_title: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
organization: NASA / LANCE (Land, Atmosphere Near real-time Capability for EOS)
claim_supported: Shows where satellites detected active fire or thermal hotspots, used for the fire exposure layer.
data_used: VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and MODIS (Terra/Aqua) active fire hotspot points: latitude, longitude, detection time, confidence.
limitation: A hotspot is a thermal anomaly, not an official fire perimeter. Small, obscured, or smoldering fires can be missed. Confidence values vary by sensor.
ethics_note: Public satellite data, no personal information involved. Must not be presented as precise, property-level fire risk.

claim_supported: Estimates population distribution for the population exposure layer.
data_used: Gridded population count, 100m resolution, top-down disaggregation of census/admin data, annual estimates 2015-2030.
limitation: Modeled estimate, not a direct census count. Accuracy can drop in fast-changing, informal, or very rural settlements.
ethics_note: Aggregated grid data, no individual-level information. Still should be generalized in the public dashboard rather than shown at very fine resolution.

claim_supported: Roads, buildings, and points of interest supporting the road/evacuation access and community assets layers.
data_used: Road network lines, building footprints, and tagged points of interest (schools, clinics, community centers).
limitation: Coverage and accuracy depend on volunteer mapping. Rural and underserved areas are often less completely mapped than urban areas.
ethics_note: Crowd-sourced public data. Do not present it as an official or complete inventory, and do not use it to tell people which evacuation route is safe.

claim_supported: Global reference boundary source for candidate-region screening only (Week 3). NOT used for the public Butte County dashboard layer; see US Census TIGER/Line below for that.
data_used: Administrative boundary polygons, levels 0-5 depending on country, version 4.1 GeoPackage format.
limitation: GADM's license is free for academic/non-commercial use only, with no redistribution or commercial use without permission. A public GitHub Pages dashboard that displays or ships this boundary data counts as redistribution, so GADM is not appropriate for the live Butte County map. Boundaries can also lag behind real political or administrative changes.
ethics_note: License restriction documented per Rhea's Week 4 review. For any US pilot region, use the public-domain US Census TIGER/Line boundary (below) instead of GADM for anything that appears in the public dashboard. GADM remains useful only for early-stage, non-published region comparison like the Week 3 matrix.

source_title: CAL FIRE FRAP Fire Perimeters (California Fire Perimeters - all)
organization: CAL FIRE Fire and Resource Assessment Program (FRAP)
claim_supported: Provides the historical Camp Fire (2018) perimeter and other Butte County fire history for the fire exposure layer and study area memo.
data_used: Statewide wildland fire perimeter polygons, updated annually each spring, available as GeoPackage/Shapefile/GeoJSON/KML/CSV.
limitation: CAL FIRE states the dataset is the most complete digital record available but is still incomplete; some historical perimeters are missing
ethics_note: so absence of a perimeter does not mean no fire occurred.
owner: Licensed Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY). Public government data, safe to use and redistribute in the dashboard with attribution to CAL FIRE FRAP.

claim_supported: Defines the Butte County study area boundary and census-tract units for the public dashboard, replacing GADM for anything that gets published.
data_used: County and census-tract boundary shapefiles/geodatabases, current vintage.
limitation: Boundaries reflect the census vintage at time of download and may not capture very recent annexations or tract redefinitions.
ethics_note: Licensed CC0 (public domain), no redistribution restriction. This is the correct boundary source for a public GitHub Pages dashboard, unlike GADM.

source_title: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) - Butte County
organization: CDC / Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR)
claim_supported: Quantifies social vulnerability (poverty, age, disability, vehicle access, language) at the census-tract level for Butte County, supporting the population exposure layer.
data_used: Census-tract level SVI composite and 4 theme scores, available for 2010-2022 vintages; county map PDF available for Butte County specifically.
limitation: SVI is a relative ranking within a state or the nation, not an absolute measure of need. It should support, not replace, local knowledge of a community.
ethics_note: US government public data. Must be described using support-focused language (need for preparedness support), not deficit or blame framing, per the project's Do/Don't rules.

source_title: EPA AirNow / Butte County Air Quality Management District
organization: US EPA (AirNow) and Butte County Air Quality Management District
claim_supported: Provides air-quality and smoke context for the smoke/AQI layer and smoke-day guide handoff to Lauren.
data_used: Station-based AQI and PM2.5 readings; Butte County AQMD operates 3 CARB monitoring stations locally plus supplemental PurpleAir sensors.
limitation: Only 3 official monitoring stations cover the whole county, so station readings may not reflect conditions in every community, especially remote areas like Concow. PurpleAir sensors are lower-cost and less rigorously calibrated.
ethics_note: Public government data via API. Should be paired with the existing non-causation note: AQI may indicate a need for precautions, not proof of health or attendance impact.

source_title: California Dept. of Education - Public School Directory
claim_supported: Provides verified school locations for Butte County as part of the community assets layer.
data_used: Geocoded point locations for all active CA public schools, with address, district, and school type; official quality-controlled geocoding process.
limitation: Directory covers public schools only; does not include private schools
column10: Official California government data, safe to use in the public dashboard. More reliable than crowd-sourced OSM tags for this specific layer, since it is government-verified rather than volunteer-mapped.

source_title: California HCAI Licensed Healthcare Facility Listing
organization: California Dept. of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) / California Dept. of Public Health
claim_supported: Provides verified hospital and clinic locations for Butte County as part of the community assets and emergency-service access layers.
data_used: Licensed and certified healthcare facility list with name, address, facility type, and license status; updated monthly.
limitation: Covers licensed facilities only, so informal or tribal health resources may be missing. Note: the previously used HIFLD Open portal for fire-station-style federal infrastructure data was shut down in August 2025 and is no longer a live source; do not reference it going forward.
ethics_note: Official California government data, safe to redistribute in the dashboard. Preferred over the earlier Healthsites.io/OSM emergency-services placeholder for Butte County specifically, since it is a verified rather than crowd-sourced source.

claim_supported: Vegetation and fuel-type patterns supporting the environmental stress layer.
data_used: 10m global land cover classification (2020 and 2021 editions), 11 classes including tree cover, shrubland, grassland, cropland, and built-up.
limitation: Only two snapshot years are available at this resolution. Classification errors are possible in mixed or transitional land cover zones.
ethics_note: Public data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Must be paired with a note that it is a snapshot, not a live or current fuel map.

claim_supported: Provides temperature and precipitation context for the environmental stress layer.
data_used: Modeled surface temperature, precipitation, and related meteorological parameters from MERRA-2 reanalysis, daily/monthly/climatology APIs, 1981 to present.
limitation: Coarse spatial resolution (about 0.5 x 0.625 degrees, roughly 50km). Modeled/reanalysis data, not ground-station observations.
ethics_note: Public data, no privacy concerns. Should be described as regional climate context, not precise local weather.

claim_supported: Vegetation health and greenness data supporting the environmental stress layer and post-fire recovery tracking.
data_used: 16-day composite NDVI and EVI, 250m resolution, Terra satellite.
limitation: Cloud cover and snow can degrade pixel quality. 16-day compositing can miss fast-changing vegetation conditions.
ethics_note: Public satellite data. Avoid over-interpreting short-term NDVI dips as proof of drought or fire risk on their own.

source_title: Healthsites.io / OSM emergency services tags (emergency services proxy)
organization: Global Healthsites Mapping Project, with OpenStreetMap Foundation, Red Cross, and Missing Maps
claim_supported: Proxy for emergency-service access supporting the service access layer.
data_used: Health facility locations (name, type, coordinates) via API/GeoJSON, supplemented with OpenStreetMap amenity=fire_station points for fire stations.
limitation: Coverage is incomplete in many rural or underserved areas, the same volunteer-mapping gap as OpenStreetMap. Does not include fire station data directly; that must come from OSM tags separately.
ethics_note: Do not publish precise coordinates of sensitive facilities without checking exposure risk. Generalize location detail where the data ethics checklist requires it.
